title: Horn-SAT: brute force over all assignments vs linear-time unit propagation
problem_statement: Given a CNF formula over Boolean variables x_1..x_n in which every clause has at most one positive literal (a Horn formula), decide whether it is satisfiable and, if it is, output its least model (the satisfying assignment whose set of true variables is contained in that of every other satisfying assignment; it exists for every satisfiable Horn formula because Horn models are closed under intersection). Clauses are a list (repetitions, repeated literals and tautologies allowed); an empty clause is unsatisfiable.

input.parameter: n = number of variables; m = number of clauses, L = total number of literal occurrences. In the V2 family H_n, m = n + 1 and L = 3n - 2.
input.size_measure: Theta(n + L) numbers (L literals of O(log n) bits each, plus n). Literals are small integers (unit-cost word operations); brute force also uses n-bit masks, one machine word for the n it can reach.

algorithms.name: brute force over all assignments
algorithms.idea: Enumerate the 2^n assignments as integers mask = 0, 1, ..., 2^n - 1 and check each clause by clause, abandoning an assignment at its first falsified clause; stop at the first satisfying assignment. For a Horn formula that first assignment is the least model: every model contains the least model bit by bit, so its mask is at least as large.
algorithms.time_complexity: O(2^n * L) always; Theta(2^n * n) = Theta(2^n * m) on the V2 family H_n, where every assignment is examined (unsatisfiable) and the 2^(n-1) assignments with x1 false pass n - 2 clauses before failing: exactly (2n + 13) 2^(n-2) - 2n - 4 literal evaluations.
algorithms.space_complexity: Theta(n + L) (the input; O(1) extra words besides the output)
algorithms.correctness: Exhaustive: every assignment is examined until one satisfies all clauses, so the satisfiability verdict is correct by definition. Least model: the models of a Horn formula are closed under intersection, so a satisfiable Horn formula has a least model M, and every model M' satisfies M subset of M', hence mask(M') >= mask(M) with equality only for M' = M; scanning masks in increasing order therefore returns M. Count on H_n (literal evaluations): the half with x1 false evaluates one literal in each of the n - 2 clauses S_j and one in F1: (n - 1) 2^(n-1). In the half with x1 true, clause S_j (scanned for j = n-1 down to 2) is reached exactly when x_{j+1..n} is non-decreasing, by (n - j + 1) 2^(j-1) assignments, which spend 2 evaluations if x_j is false and 3 if it is true, 5 (n - j + 1) 2^(j-2) in total; summed over j this is 15 * 2^(n-2) - 5n - 5. The n assignments that pass every S_j then spend 3 evaluations on F1 and F2, and the all-true one 1 more on G: 3n + 1. Total (2n + 13) 2^(n-2) - 2n - 4, checked against the counts for every n = 3..16.

algorithms.name: unit propagation with clause counters (Dowling-Gallier)
algorithms.idea: Read each clause y_1 AND ... AND y_k -> h as an implication (h absent for a goal clause). Keep, per clause, a counter of negative literals whose variable is not yet true and, per variable, the list of clauses in which it occurs negatively. Start from the facts (counter 0), and each time a variable becomes true decrement the counters of its clauses; a clause whose counter reaches 0 makes its head true, or proves unsatisfiability if it is a goal.
algorithms.pseudocode:
for each clause c: head[c] = positive variable or 0; counter[c] = #negative literals; occurs[v] += [c] for each NOT v in c
  if counter[c] == 0: if head[c] == 0: return UNSAT else push head[c]
while queue: v = pop
  if v already true: continue; set v true
  for c in occurs[v]: counter[c] -= 1
    if counter[c] == 0: if head[c] == 0: return UNSAT; if head[c] not true: push head[c]
return the true variables
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n + L) on every input: every variable is set true at most once, so every negative literal occurrence is decremented at most once and every clause fires at most once. On H_n exactly 12n - 7 counted operations.
algorithms.correctness: Dowling & Gallier 1984. Every variable set true is true in every model (induction on the order of setting: its clause's other variables are already true), so a firing goal clause proves unsatisfiability. If propagation ends without that, every clause is satisfied by 'exactly the derived variables are true': a clause whose negative variables are all true has fired and made its head true; any other clause has a false negative literal. That assignment is contained in every model, so it is the least model. Count on H_n by inspection: building costs 7n - 5 counted operations (3 per negative literal: comparison, negation, index; 1 per positive literal; 1 for the fact test of F1) and propagation 5n - 2 (3 per variable set true, 2 per firing clause with a head; the head 0 of the goal G is a plain integer, not counted), confirmed for every n = 3..300 and at the V2 sizes.

relationship: Same problem. Brute force is exponential, Theta(2^n * m) on the worst-case family; unit propagation is linear, Theta(n + L), so Horn-SAT is in P. The structure used: a Horn clause is an implication with a single conclusion, so the set of forced variables can be computed forward, each clause firing at most once. Boundary: Horn formulas are one of Schaefer's (1978) tractable classes of Boolean constraints, while satisfiability of general CNF formulas is NP-complete (Cook 1971). See also pairs/two-sat-brute-force-vs-scc (another Schaefer class) and pairs/3sat-brute-force-vs-schoening.

verification.method: V1: both implementations return the same least model (compared with ==) on n = 0..8, 10, 12, 14 (brute force up to n = 14; unit propagation also on n = 50, 300), 4 formulas per size: random Horn CNF at clause/variable ratios 0.5-4 with widths 1-4, planted derivation chains (satisfiable) and the same chains with a goal on derived variables (unsatisfiable), edge cases with repeated literals, tautologies, unit goals and empty clauses, the V2 family under random renaming, and definite-clause formulas. The independent check() recomputes the derived set by naive forward chaining (repeated full passes; no counters or occurrence lists) and accepts an assignment only if it equals that set and satisfies every clause, and None only if the derived set violates a clause (a proof of unsatisfiability); for n <= 10 it also cross-checks the verdict by exhaustive search. Oracle control (experiments/2026-10-06f_entries_horn_sat.py): on 1040 seeded instances (n = 0..12) it accepts all 1040 correct outputs and rejects all 2816 wrong ones (465 flipped bits, 271 strictly larger models, 505 None for satisfiable formulas, 535 all-false assignments for unsatisfiable formulas, 1040 wrong lengths). V2 (exact counts, RESEARCH_LOG RL-047 method): the deterministic unsatisfiable family H_n = (NOT x1 OR NOT x_j OR x_{j+1}) for j = n-1 down to 2, then (x1), (NOT x1 OR x2), (NOT x_n), built from a harness literal type CountingLit that counts every operation on input-derived values; the implementations are unchanged. Brute force: exactly 6 * ((2n + 13) 2^(n-2) - 2n - 4) operations (6 per literal evaluation; derived by hand, checked for every n = 3..16); fit against (2n + 13) 2^n - 8n - 16 on n = 8..16: alpha = 1.000 (tol 0.02); rivals 2^n (alpha 1.081) and n^2 2^n (0.865) rejected. Unit propagation: exactly 12n - 7 operations (by inspection; checked for every n = 3..300 and at the V2 sizes); fit against 12n - 7 on n = 1000..32000: alpha = 1.000; rivals n log n (0.895) and n^2 (0.500) rejected, so the counts also resolve the log factor. On the same family naive forward chaining needs exactly n full passes (checked for n = 3..200), i.e. Theta(n^2) clause visits.

caveats: Brute force stops at the first satisfying assignment (for a Horn formula, the least model), so on satisfiable formulas its cost depends on where the least model lies in mask order: a formula with no facts is satisfied by mask 0 after one pass over the clauses. The V2 family is therefore unsatisfiable, and its clauses are ordered so that half of all assignments pass n - 2 clauses before failing; with clauses in random order a random assignment fails early and the count grows like 2^n, not m 2^n. The worst case Theta(2^n * L) for general L needs repeated or long clauses; the family shows it for m = Theta(n). The fitted brute-force cost is the exact count's form: the bare n 2^n gives alpha = 0.961 at n <= 16, outside the 0.02 band (experiment, section 5). The unit-propagation count measures operations on input-derived values: the counter decrements use plain clause indices and are not counted, but each negative literal occurrence is decremented at most once and costs at least one counted operation when it is read, so the uncounted part is O(L). Counted operations measure Python-level work, not machine instructions.
notes: Horn-SAT is the satisfiability problem of one of Schaefer's tractable classes; 2-SAT (pairs/two-sat-brute-force-vs-scc) and XOR-SAT (pairs/xor-sat-brute-force-vs-gaussian-elimination) are two others. Dual-Horn formulas (at most one negative literal per clause) are handled by the same algorithm after negating every variable. Minoux (1988) gives a simplified linear-time unit-resolution algorithm for Horn formulae; the implementation here follows the counter scheme described above.
